about: Every settings row the interface can show, made by ps5/tools/settings-inventory.py from the code (ps5/tests/bigpicture/inventory). The no-loss test compares the code with this file; bless writes it.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Settings shown
rows.desc: How many settings are shown. Normal covers what most people need, Advanced adds finer options, and Expert shows everything, including options that can stop games from working. Press Triangle anywhere in Settings to switch.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Pause when a controller disconnects
rows.desc: Pauses the emulator when a controller with bindings is disconnected.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Warn about unsafe settings
rows.desc: Displays warnings when settings are enabled which may break games.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Circle chooses, Cross goes back
rows.desc: Swaps the Cross and Circle buttons in all menus, as on Japanese consoles.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Skin
rows.desc: Changes the colours and style of the interface. Carbon uses a black background, which suits OLED screens.

choices.name: Chakra (Modern and accessible · after Chakra UI)
Humane (Clean and readable · after Semantic UI)

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Accent colour
rows.desc: The colour used to highlight the selected item and switched-on options.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Background
rows.desc: What is shown behind the menus: a still or animated background, the selected game's artwork, or your own pictures from the "backgrounds" folder.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: My pictures: each stays for
rows.desc: How long each of your pictures is shown before the next one.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: My pictures: made darker by
rows.desc: Darkens your pictures so the text on top of them stays readable.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: My pictures: look into the folder again
rows.desc: Checks the folder again for new pictures.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Motion
rows.desc: How much the interface animates. All: animated background and sliding menus. Less: fades only. None: no animation.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Start-up animation
rows.desc: Plays the animated logo when Crux2 starts. Press any button to skip it.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Which start-up
rows.desc: Chooses which of the four start-up animations plays. Random picks a different one each time.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Interface size
rows.desc: Makes the whole interface smaller so more fits on screen.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Text size
rows.desc: Makes the text larger or smaller without changing the rest of the interface.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: High contrast
rows.desc: Makes text brighter and outlines stronger.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Colours for colour blindness
rows.desc: Uses blue and orange instead of green and red to show success and failure.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Startup video
rows.desc: Plays Crux2's short video when it starts, in place of the start-up animation, with the start-up sound's volume. Press any button to skip it. Needs the start-up animation on and Motion set to All.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Interface sounds
rows.desc: Plays sounds when you move and select in the menus.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Music
rows.desc: Plays your own music in the menus. Put WAV, MP3, OGG or FLAC files in the "music" folder.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Start-up sound
rows.desc: Plays a sound with the start-up animation. Put your own startup.wav in the title folder to replace it.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Go dark when nothing is pressed
rows.desc: Dims the screen after this long without input, then turns it black. Press any button to wake it.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Then the black screen with the mark
rows.desc: Shows a black screen with a moving logo after the screen dims. Off: the screen only dims.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Move everything a little
rows.desc: Moves the whole picture by a few pixels every couple of minutes to reduce the risk of burn-in on OLED screens.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Fade the hints
rows.desc: Fades the button hints at the bottom of the screen when nothing has been pressed for a while.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Darken the game when nothing is pressed
rows.desc: Dims the game after this long without input. Pressing any button brings it back.

rows.heading: GAME SCANNING
rows.label: Scan for games
rows.desc: Looks for new games in the games folder, on USB drives and on network shares.

rows.heading: GAME SCANNING
rows.label: Scan again from nothing
rows.desc: Rescans all game files, not just new ones. Use it if a game shows the wrong title. Can take a while on a network share.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Library view
rows.desc: How games are shown in the library. You can also switch views with the touch pad.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: A picture of play behind the shelves
rows.desc: Shows a screenshot of the selected game behind the shelves.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Group the discs of a game
rows.desc: Shows a game that has several discs as one entry. It starts from the disc you played last.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: English titles
rows.desc: For games with both a title in the game's native language and one in English, prefer the English title.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Fetch the games' pictures
rows.desc: Downloads title screens and screenshots for your games from libretro's collection.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: USB drives
rows.desc: Shows a USB tab for games in a folder named Crux2 or PS2 on a USB drive.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Disc drives
rows.desc: Checks the console's disc drive and USB DVD drives for PS2 discs and shows them on their own tab. USB DVD drives can also read PS2 CDs.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Read the disc into memory while playing
rows.desc: Copies the whole disc into memory while you play, so the drive is no longer needed. Off: only recently read data is kept.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Keep the disc turning
rows.desc: Reads from the disc every 20 seconds so the drive doesn't spin down during play.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Make an image of the disc
rows.desc: Copies your disc to an ISO, CHD or CSO image on the console, a USB drive or a network share.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Eject a disc
rows.desc: Unlocks and opens a disc drive's tray.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Share the covers
rows.desc: Syncs covers both ways with the backup location, so all your devices have them.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download covers automatically
rows.desc: Downloads missing covers from libretro's collection after each scan.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Fetch game pictures automatically
rows.desc: Downloads title screens and screenshots for your games after each scan.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Look up what each game is
rows.desc: Shows a short description of the game in the drive, looked up on Wikipedia.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Look the games up again
rows.desc: Clears the stored game descriptions so they are looked up again.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download the missing covers now
rows.desc: Tries again to download covers for every game without one.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download cheats for all games
rows.desc: Downloads cheats for all your games from the cheat collections on GitHub. Cheats stay off until you enable them for a game.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download PCSX2's patches
rows.desc: Downloads PCSX2's game patches (widescreen, no-interlacing, 60 fps and more) from GitHub.

rows.heading: GAME FOLDERS
rows.label: Add a game folder
rows.desc: Pick any folder on a USB drive, a network share or the console. Its games, and those in the folders inside it, join the library where they are: nothing is moved or copied.

rows.heading: GAME FOLDERS
rows.label: /mnt/usb0/games
rows.desc: A game folder you added. Press to take it off the list: its games leave the library, the files stay where they are.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Kind
rows.desc: SMB for a Windows PC and most NAS; NFS for a NAS or a Linux PC that shares its folders that way.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Server
rows.desc: The PC or NAS: found on this network (those answering on SMB's or NFS's port), its address on the number pad, or its name typed.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Share and folder
rows.desc: The share and the folder in it with the games: Games/PS2. Picked from the server's list, or typed.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Name
rows.desc: How the share is shown in the library. Left empty: its last folder.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: User
rows.desc: An account of the share's own. Left empty: the shares' account below (guest for an open share).

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Password
rows.desc: The password of the share's own account.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Test the share
rows.desc: Connects to it and reads its folder, and says what went wrong if it can't: the address, the port, the account, the share's name or the folder. Nothing is saved.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Add the share
rows.desc: Connects to it now and adds its games to the library; network.cfg keeps it for the next start.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Cancel
rows.desc: Leaves the share as it was.

rows.heading: NETWORK SHARES
rows.label: Add a network share
rows.desc: A folder of games on a PC or NAS, read over the network as the games play (SMB or NFS). Set up here with the on-screen keyboard and number pad: network.cfg is written for you.

rows.heading: NETWORK SHARES
rows.label: The shares' account
rows.desc: The user and password for the SMB shares without an account of their own: guest and no password for an open share.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: BIOS
rows.desc: Choose the folder for BIOS, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Memory cards
rows.desc: Choose the folder for Memory cards, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Save states
rows.desc: Choose the folder for Save states, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Screenshots and GS dumps
rows.desc: Choose the folder for Screenshots and GS dumps, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Cheats
rows.desc: Choose the folder for Cheats, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Covers
rows.desc: Choose the folder for Covers, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Texture replacements
rows.desc: Choose the folder for Texture replacements, or go back to the default. Takes effect for the next game started.

rows.heading: THE PLAYSTATION 2'S OWN MENU
rows.label: Start the PlayStation 2 menu
rows.desc: Starts the PS2 BIOS without a game, to use the memory card browser and System Configuration.

rows.heading: BIOS SELECTION
rows.label: BIOS
rows.desc: The PS2 BIOS, which every game needs. Use a dump from your own console.

rows.heading: BIOS SELECTION
rows.label: Free BIOS when none of my own is found
rows.desc: Uses OpenPS2BIOS, an open-source BIOS included with Crux2, when no BIOS of your own is found. Experimental: many games don't get past their menus.

rows.heading: LANGUAGE
rows.label: Console language
rows.desc: The language games are told the PS2 is set to. Many European games use it to choose their language. Your BIOS settings are not changed.

rows.heading: OPTIONS AND PATCHES
rows.label: Fast boot
rows.desc: Patches the BIOS to skip the console's boot animation.

rows.heading: OPTIONS AND PATCHES
rows.label: Fast-forward to the game
rows.desc: Removes emulation speed throttle until the game starts to reduce startup time.

rows.heading: SPEED CONTROL
rows.label: Normal speed
rows.desc: Sets the speed when running without fast forwarding.

rows.heading: SPEED CONTROL
rows.label: Fast-forward speed
rows.desc: Sets the speed when using the fast forward hotkey.

rows.heading: SPEED CONTROL
rows.label: Slow-motion speed
rows.desc: Sets the speed when using the slow motion hotkey.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: EE cycle rate
rows.desc: Underclocks or overclocks the emulated Emotion Engine CPU.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: EE cycle skipping
rows.desc: Makes the emulated Emotion Engine skip cycles. Helps a small subset of games like SOTC. Most of the time it's harmful to performance.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Multi-threaded VU1 (MTVU)
rows.desc: Generally a speedup on CPUs with 4 or more cores. Safe for most games, but a few are incompatible and may hang.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Thread pinning
rows.desc: How the emulator's threads are placed on the CPU cores. Anywhere is best for most games. Try another option if a game is slow at every resolution.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Graphics driver on a core of its own
rows.desc: With "Cores of their own", moves the graphics driver's thread off the GS thread's core, so the GS thread has its core to itself. Turn it off if a game runs slower with it. Takes effect the next time Crux2 starts.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Fast disc access
rows.desc: Fast disc access, shorter loading times. Check HDLoader compatibility lists for games that are known to have issues with this.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Load the whole disc into memory
rows.desc: Loads the disc image into RAM before starting the virtual machine.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Cheats
rows.desc: Enables loading cheats from pnach files.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Host file system
rows.desc: Allows games and homebrew to access files and folders directly in the title folder.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Refresh rate
rows.desc: Sends 120 Hz to the TV if it supports it. Needed for frame generation to 120 fps and black frame insertion. Hold L1 and R1 while Crux2 starts to use 60 Hz once.

choices.name: 120 Hz when the television has it

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Variable refresh (VRR)
rows.desc: With 120 Hz on a TV that has VRR, each frame is shown as soon as it is ready instead of at the next fixed refresh: smoother when a game drops below full speed. Takes effect the next time Crux2 starts. Experimental.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Frame pacing
rows.desc: By the screen: frames are paced by the display's refresh, the smoothest option. By the clock: for games whose frame rate the display can't match.

choices.name: By the clock, in step with the screen
By the clock, at the game's own rate

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Frames queued for the display
rows.desc: Sets the number of frames which can be queued.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Queue frames while the game is behind
rows.desc: When a game runs below full speed, lets up to 2 frames wait in the queue so the emulator and the graphics thread can work at the same time. Can add a little input lag while the game is slow.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Show a frame as it begins
rows.desc: Displays the newest frame immediately at the beginning of the frame raster time, instead of at the end. Can reduce perceived input lag, but may cause problems with some games, such as Soulcalibur II and Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance II.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Skip repeated frames
rows.desc: Skips displaying frames that don't change in 25/30fps games. Can improve speed, but increase input lag/make frame pacing worse.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Black frame insertion
rows.desc: At 120 Hz, inserts a black frame after each frame to reduce motion blur. Makes the picture darker. Can't be used together with frame generation.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate floating point (FPU)
rows.desc: Does the FPU's maths exactly as the PS2 does, for games whose physics or AI go wrong otherwise. Slower. From PCSX2 Reliquary. On by default for the games known to need it.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate floating point (VU0)
rows.desc: Does VU0's maths exactly as the PS2 does. Usually needed with the FPU one. Slower. From PCSX2 Reliquary. On by default for the games known to need it.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate floating point (VU1)
rows.desc: Does VU1's maths exactly as the PS2 does, for some graphics errors. Much slower: use it only when a game needs it. From PCSX2 Reliquary.

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Set the clock by hand
rows.desc: Manually set a real-time clock to use for the virtual PlayStation 2 instead of using your OS' system clock.

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Year
rows.desc: Calendar year for the virtual PS2 RTC.

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Month
rows.desc: Month of the year (1-12).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Day
rows.desc: Day of the month (1-31).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Hour
rows.desc: Hour of the day (0-23).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Minute
rows.desc: Minute of the hour (0-59).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Second
rows.desc: Second of the minute (0-59).

rows.heading: PATCHES
rows.label: A patch
rows.desc: What the patch does.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: A cheat
rows.desc: What the cheat does.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: FPU multiply hack
rows.desc: For Tales of Destiny.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Software renderer for videos
rows.desc: Needed for some games with complex FMV rendering.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Skip videos
rows.desc: Skips videos/FMVs in games to avoid game hanging/freezes.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Preload TLB hack
rows.desc: To avoid TLB miss on Goemon.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: EE timing hack
rows.desc: General-purpose timing hack. Known to affect following games: Digital Devil Saga, SSX.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Instant DMA hack
rows.desc: Good for cache emulation problems. Known to affect following games: Fire Pro Wrestling Z.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: OPH flag hack
rows.desc: Known to affect following games: Bleach Blade Battlers, Growlanser II and III, Wizardry.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Emulate the GIF FIFO
rows.desc: Correct but slower. Known to affect the following games: FIFA Street 2.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: DMA busy hack
rows.desc: Known to affect following games: Mana Khemia 1, Metal Saga, Pilot Down Behind Enemy Lines.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Delay VIF1 stalls
rows.desc: For SOCOM 2 HUD and Spy Hunter loading hang.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Emulate the VIF FIFO
rows.desc: Simulate VIF1 FIFO read ahead. Known to affect following games: Test Drive Unlimited, Transformers.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Full VU0 synchronisation
rows.desc: Forces tight VU0 sync on every COP2 instruction.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU I bit hack
rows.desc: Avoids constant recompilation in some games. Known to affect the following games: Scarface The World is Yours, Crash Tag Team Racing.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU add hack
rows.desc: For Tri-Ace Games: Star Ocean 3, Radiata Stories, Valkyrie Profile 2.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU overflow hack
rows.desc: To check for possible float overflows (Superman Returns).

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU sync
rows.desc: Run behind. To avoid sync problems when reading or writing VU registers.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU XGKick sync
rows.desc: Use accurate timing for VU XGKicks (slower).

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Count frames by blits
rows.desc: Use alternative method to calculate internal FPS to avoid false readings in some games.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Use cheats
rows.desc: Enables loading cheats from pnach files.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Those of other versions of the game too
rows.desc: Also lists cheats and patches made for other versions of the game. They may not work.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Download cheats for this game
rows.desc: Downloads cheats for this game from the cheat collections on GitHub.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Type a cheat in
rows.desc: Enter a raw cheat code: a name first, then one code line at a time. Encrypted codes won't work.

rows.heading: PATCHES
rows.label: Those of other versions of the game too
rows.desc: Also lists cheats and patches made for other versions of the game. They may not work.

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Fastest
rows.desc: The PlayStation 2's own resolution, nothing extra: for a game that is slow at any setting

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Balanced
rows.desc: Drawn at about 1080p, a little sharper textures: the choice for most games

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Sharpest
rows.desc: Drawn at about 1440p and brought to 4K with AMD FSR 1, the sharpest textures: for a game with speed to spare

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Automatic quality
rows.desc: Lowers the internal resolution when the game can't hold full speed, and raises it again when there's room. Doesn't help when the CPU is the bottleneck.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Renderer
rows.desc: Selects how the emulated GS is drawn: Hardware uses the GPU, Software uses the CPU like the PS2 did (slow but accurate), paraLLEl-GS emulates the GS on the GPU at high accuracy.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS samples
rows.desc: How many samples paraLLEl-GS takes per pixel. More samples give a smoother, sharper picture but need more GPU power.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS at twice the size
rows.desc: Renders at twice the PS2's resolution when using 4 or more samples. Sharper, but needs more GPU power.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS sharp 2-D
rows.desc: Applies super-sampling to text, menus and other 2D elements. Sharper, but may cause seams in some games.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS hands work over as it goes (experimental)
rows.desc: Sends work to the GPU while the frame is still being recorded. Can help games that read back the screen. Experimental.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS full-detail effects
rows.desc: Keeps full detail in effects that render to a texture, such as blur, glow and depth of field. Needs more GPU power.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS pictures shared with the graphics device (experimental)
rows.desc: Passes paraLLEl-GS frames to the display without copying them on the CPU. Experimental.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Aspect ratio
rows.desc: Selects the aspect ratio to display the game content at.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: FMV aspect ratio override
rows.desc: Selects the aspect ratio for display when a FMV is detected as playing.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Beside a 4:3 picture
rows.desc: What fills the sides of the screen when the game is 4:3. Dark grey wears an OLED screen more evenly than black.

choices.name: A blurred copy of the picture

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Deinterlacing
rows.desc: Determines the deinterlacing method to be used on the interlaced screen of the emulated console. Automatic should be able to correctly deinterlace most games, but if you see visibly shaky graphics, try one of the other options.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Bilinear filtering
rows.desc: Smooths out the image when upscaling the console to the screen.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Widescreen patches
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies widescreen patches on game start. Can cause issues.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: No-interlacing patches
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies no-interlacing patches on game start. Can cause issues.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Widescreen patch
rows.desc: Applies this game's widescreen patch, if one exists.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: No-interlacing patch
rows.desc: Applies this game's no-interlacing patch, if one exists.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Anti-blur
rows.desc: Enables internal Anti-Blur hacks. Less accurate than PS2 rendering but will make a lot of games look less blurry.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Integer scaling
rows.desc: Adds padding to the display area to ensure that the ratio between pixels on the host to pixels in the console is an integer number. May result in a sharper image in some 2D games.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Screen offsets
rows.desc: Enables PCRTC Offsets which position the screen as the game requests.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Show overscan
rows.desc: Enables the option to show the overscan area on games which draw more than the safe area of the screen.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Disable interlace offset
rows.desc: Disables interlacing offset which may reduce blurring in some situations.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Vertical stretch
rows.desc: Increases or decreases the virtual picture size vertically.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop left
rows.desc: Crops the image, while respecting aspect ratio.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop top
rows.desc: Crops the image, while respecting aspect ratio.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop right
rows.desc: Crops the image, while respecting aspect ratio.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop bottom
rows.desc: Crops the image, while respecting aspect ratio.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Output resolution
rows.desc: The resolution sent to the TV. Lower it on a 1080p or 1440p TV to save GPU power.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: HDR
rows.desc: Sends the picture to the TV as HDR10, with the game's brightest parts brighter. Needs the console's own HDR setting on and a TV that takes HDR; otherwise the picture stays SDR.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Peak brightness
rows.desc: For HDR: how bright the game's brightest parts (the sky, lights, fire) become. Set it near the TV's peak. Off: the SDR picture as it is, at the white level.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: White level
rows.desc: For HDR: how bright white is, the menus' and the game's ordinary whites. 203 nits is HDR's reference; raise it if the picture looks dim.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Adjust HDR brightness
rows.desc: A test screen: the X in a square raised until it vanishes sets the peak, then a grey scale sets the white level.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Internal resolution
rows.desc: Multiplies the render resolution by the specified factor (upscaling).

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Upscaling and sharpening
rows.desc: Off uses the internal resolution as it is. FSR 1 renders the game at a lower resolution and upscales it with AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution; CAS sharpens the image with FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Sharpness
rows.desc: Determines the intensity the sharpening effect in CAS post-processing.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Texture filtering
rows.desc: Selects where bilinear filtering is utilized when rendering textures.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Trilinear filtering
rows.desc: Selects where trilinear filtering is utilized when rendering textures.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Anisotropic filtering
rows.desc: Reduces texture aliasing at extreme viewing angles.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Dithering
rows.desc: Selects the type of dithering applies when the game requests it.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Blending accuracy
rows.desc: Determines the level of accuracy when emulating blend modes not supported by the host graphics API.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Mipmapping
rows.desc: Enables mipmapping, which some games require to render correctly. Mipmapping uses progressively lower resolution variants of textures at progressively further distances to reduce processing load and avoid visual artifacts.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Accurate alpha test
rows.desc: Enables accurate alpha testing, which some games require to render correctly. This may require more draw calls and result in a speed penalty.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: AA1
rows.desc: Enables AA1 (PS2 antialiasing), which some games require to render correctly. This may result in a heavy performance penalty.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Rasterizer ordered view
rows.desc: Enables Rasterizer Ordered View (ROV), which allows feedback loops to be executed with fewer draw calls. Can improve performance in feedback heavy games with higher accuracy settings.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Software renderer threads
rows.desc: Number of threads to use in addition to the main GS thread for rasterization.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Software auto flush
rows.desc: Force a primitive flush when a framebuffer is also an input texture.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Software mipmapping
rows.desc: Enables mipmapping, which some games require to render correctly. Mipmapping uses progressively lower resolution variants of textures at progressively further distances to reduce processing load and avoid visual artifacts.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Manual hardware renderer fixes
rows.desc: Disables automatic hardware fixes, allowing you to set fixes manually.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: CPU sprite render size
rows.desc: The maximum target memory width that will allow the CPU Sprite Renderer to activate on.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: CPU sprite render level
rows.desc: Determines filter level for CPU sprite render.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Software CLUT render
rows.desc: Tries to detect when a game is drawing its own color palette and then renders it in software, instead of on the GPU.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: GPU target CLUT
rows.desc: Tries to detect when a game is drawing its own color palette and then renders it on the GPU with special handling.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Skip draws from
rows.desc: Completely skips drawing surfaces from the starting index up to the ending index.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Skip draws to
rows.desc: Completely skips drawing surfaces from the starting index up to the ending index.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Auto flush
rows.desc: Forces a primitive flush when a framebuffer is also an input texture. Fixes some processing effects such as the shadows in the Jak series and radiosity in GTA:SA.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Framebuffer conversion on the processor
rows.desc: Convert 4-bit and 8-bit framebuffer on the CPU instead of the GPU.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: No depth conversion
rows.desc: Disable the support of depth buffers in the texture cache.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: No safe features
rows.desc: This option disables multiple safe features.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: No render fixes
rows.desc: This option disables game-specific render fixes.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Preload frame data
rows.desc: Uploads GS data when rendering a new frame to reproduce some effects accurately.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: No partial invalidation
rows.desc: Removes texture cache entries when there is any intersection, rather than only the intersected areas.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Texture inside a render target
rows.desc: Allows the texture cache to reuse as an input texture the inner portion of a previous framebuffer.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Read targets when closing
rows.desc: Flushes all targets in the texture cache back to local memory when shutting down.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Estimate texture region
rows.desc: Attempts to reduce the texture size when games do not set it themselves (e.g. Snowblind games).

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Draw buffering
rows.desc: Attempts to reduce draw calls in games which do heavy context switching for blending purposes.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Rewrite large ST
rows.desc: Rewrites large texture coordinates to avoid stretched or wrong textures in some games.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Target page rearranging
rows.desc: Rearranges memory pages of a target if the game changes the layout at that current VRAM address.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Palette conversion on the graphics chip
rows.desc: When enabled GPU converts colormap-textures, otherwise the CPU will. It is a trade-off between GPU and CPU.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Limit depth to 24 bits
rows.desc: Truncate 32-bit depth values to 24 bits. Helps games struggling with Z-fighting.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Half pixel offset
rows.desc: Might fix some misaligned fog, bloom, or blend effect.

choices.name: Align to native, with texture offset

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Native scaling
rows.desc: Emulates native PS2 coordinate scaling behavior when upscaling to reduce misalignment artifacts and seams in games that draw custom 2D elements.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Round sprite
rows.desc: Adjusts sprite coordinates.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Bilinear dirty upscale
rows.desc: Can smooth out textures due to be bilinear filtered when upscaling. E.g. Brave sun glare.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Texture offset X
rows.desc: Adjusts target texture offsets.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Texture offset Y
rows.desc: Adjusts target texture offsets.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Align sprite
rows.desc: Fixes issues with upscaling (vertical lines) in some games.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Merge sprite
rows.desc: Replaces post-processing multiple paving sprites by a single fat sprite. It reduces various upscaling lines.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Even sprite positions
rows.desc: Lowers the GS precision to avoid gaps between pixels when upscaling. Fixes the text on Wild Arms games.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Palette draws at native resolution
rows.desc: Forces palette texture draws to render at native resolution.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Load textures
rows.desc: Loads replacement textures where available and user-provided.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Asynchronous texture loading
rows.desc: Loads replacement textures on a worker thread, reducing microstutter when replacements are enabled.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Precache replacements
rows.desc: Preloads all replacement textures to memory. Not necessary with asynchronous loading.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: HD texture packs
rows.desc: Opens the texture pack manager: the packs on this console, the USB drives and the shares, by game. Download packs from the Internet Archive, one after another, and move or delete them. Packs can be several GB.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Stop the download
rows.desc: Stops the download. Files already unpacked are kept.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Download connections
rows.desc: How many connections a texture pack is downloaded over at once, each bringing a piece of it. More is faster while the Internet Archive slows each connection down; 1 is one stream, as before. Takes effect with the next download.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Dump textures
rows.desc: Dumps replaceable textures to disk. Will reduce performance.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Dump mipmaps
rows.desc: Includes mipmaps when dumping textures.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Dump FMV textures
rows.desc: Allows texture dumping when FMVs are active. You should not enable this.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Anti-aliasing
rows.desc: Smooths the jagged edges of the picture. FXAA: quick, a little soft. SMAA: sharper edges, a little GPU time. SSAA: the game drawn larger than the screen and made screen-sized, the least shimmer; choosing it raises the internal resolution to about one and a half times the screen's (8x at 4K) and turns FSR 1 off, and costs the most. SSAA + SMAA: SSAA, then SMAA over it for the edges it leaves.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: SSAA filter
rows.desc: How SSAA makes the larger picture screen-sized. Soft: every pixel it covers averaged, the least shimmer. Sharp: a Lanczos filter, crisper edges.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: TV shader
rows.desc: Applies a shader which replicates the visual effects of different styles of television sets.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Look (shader preset)
rows.desc: Makes the picture look like an old TV, with CRT shaders, composite or S-Video signal effects and film grain.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: A look of your own
rows.desc: Loads a libretro shader preset (.slangp) from a "shaders" folder on a USB drive or in the title folder.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Debanding
rows.desc: Smooths the colour bands in skies, fog and dark gradients; edges and detail are kept. Low: the fine steps of 32-bit colour. High: the wider ones of 16-bit colour.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Colour filter on the game
rows.desc: For colour blindness: moves the colours you may not tell apart to ones you can. Red-weak and green-weak help with reds and greens, blue-weak with blues and yellows. The game's picture only; the menus' colours are under Interface.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Shade boost
rows.desc: Enables brightness/contrast/gamma/saturation adjustment.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Brightness
rows.desc: Adjusts brightness. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Contrast
rows.desc: Adjusts contrast. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Gamma
rows.desc: Adjusts gamma. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Saturation
rows.desc: Adjusts saturation. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Frame generation
rows.desc: Generates extra frames between the game's own, so a 30 fps game is shown at 60 fps. Adds a little input lag and can cause smearing on fast movement.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Frame generation method
rows.desc: How the extra frames are made. Crux2's own: its motion search. AMD FSR 3 optical flow: handles small, fast movement better, and keeps a score or a map still. MihawkGen: Mihawk's small trained network, which looks at the two pictures only and leaves what did not move exactly as it was.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Optical flow quality
rows.desc: Higher quality needs more GPU power.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: No frame generation during videos
rows.desc: Turns frame generation off while the game plays a video.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Steady 30
rows.desc: Takes the game's pictures two vsyncs apart at the most, so a game that goes between 30 and 60 a second is shown at an even 30 that frame generation makes 60 (120 at 120 Hz). For games that cannot hold 60.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Show the movement
rows.desc: For checking frame generation, not for playing: the made frames show what AMD FSR 3 optical flow decided for each pixel instead of the picture (red both frames, green the newer alone, blue the older alone, grey the two mixed). Takes effect the next time a game starts.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Keep read render targets uncompressed (experimental)
rows.desc: Keeps render targets uncompressed when glow and flare effects read them. Can be faster in some games. Experimental; takes effect the next time a game starts.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Render targets without compression (experimental)
rows.desc: Creates render targets without colour compression. Can be faster or slower depending on the game. Experimental; takes effect the next time a game starts.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Leave out barriers with nothing to wait for
rows.desc: Skips GPU waits when nothing has been drawn since the last one. Turn off if effects look wrong. Takes effect the next time a game starts.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Reuse copies of the picture
rows.desc: Reuses copies of the screen for glow and blur effects when nothing has changed. Turn off if an effect looks a frame behind. Takes effect the next time a game starts.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Keep the ordered view's render passes
rows.desc: Keeps draws that use the rasterizer ordered view in the same render pass. Much less CPU work in scenes with many lights. Takes effect the next time a game starts.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Hardware download mode
rows.desc: Changes synchronization behavior for GS downloads.

choices.name: No readbacks (the threads run in step)

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Texture preloading
rows.desc: Uploads full textures to the GPU on use, rather than only the utilized regions. Can improve performance in some games.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Extended upscaling multipliers
rows.desc: Displays additional, very high upscaling multipliers dependent on GPU and driver capability.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Internal resolution above 12x
rows.desc: Multiplies the render resolution by the specified factor (upscaling).

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Override texture barriers
rows.desc: Forces texture barrier functionality to the specified value.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Extra barriers with the ordered view
rows.desc: Forces extra barriers when using ROV with Vulkan to fix graphical issues present in some games and hardware configurations.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable shader cache
rows.desc: Prevents the loading and saving of shaders/pipelines to disk.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable vertex shader expand
rows.desc: Falls back to the CPU for expanding sprites/lines.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Spin CPU during readbacks
rows.desc: Does useless work on the CPU during readbacks to prevent it from going into powersave modes. May improve performance during readbacks but with a significant increase in power usage.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Spin GPU during readbacks
rows.desc: Submits useless work to the GPU during readbacks to prevent it from going into powersave modes. May improve performance during readbacks but with a significant increase in power usage.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable framebuffer fetch
rows.desc: Prevents the usage of framebuffer fetch when supported by host GPU.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Use blit swap chain
rows.desc: Uses a blit presentation model instead of flipping when using the Direct3D 11 graphics API. Has no effect on the PS5.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: NTSC frame rate
rows.desc: The frame rate used for NTSC games.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: PAL frame rate
rows.desc: The frame rate used for PAL games.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD scale
rows.desc: Scales the size of the onscreen OSD from 50% to 500%.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD margin
rows.desc: Sets the distance in pixels from the edges of the screen for OSD elements.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD messages position
rows.desc: Determines where on-screen display messages are positioned.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD performance position
rows.desc: Position of a variety of on-screen performance data points as selected by the user.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: Bold figures
rows.desc: Draws OSD text with heavier weight for improved readability.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: Move the figures from corner to corner
rows.desc: Moves the on-screen figures to another corner every five minutes to prevent burn-in.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: Style
rows.desc: Crux2: one panel with sections and a frame-time graph. PCSX2: PCSX2's own lines of text.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Speed percentages
rows.desc: Shows the current emulation speed of the system as a percentage.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: FPS
rows.desc: Shows the number of internal video frames displayed per second by the system.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: VPS
rows.desc: Shows the number of Vsyncs performed per second by the system.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Resolution
rows.desc: Shows the internal resolution of the game.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: CPU usage
rows.desc: Shows the host's CPU utilization based on threads.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: GPU usage
rows.desc: Shows the host's GPU utilization.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Frame times
rows.desc: Displays a graph showing the average frametimes.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Hardware info
rows.desc: Shows the current system CPU and GPU information.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Statistics
rows.desc: Shows statistics about the emulated GS such as primitives and draw calls.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: GPU statistics
rows.desc: Shows GPU vertex shader and pixels shader invocations.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Indicators
rows.desc: Shows icon indicators for emulation states such as Pausing, Turbo, Fast-Forward, and Slow-Motion.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Settings
rows.desc: Displays various settings and the current values of those settings in the bottom-right corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Patches
rows.desc: Shows the amount of currently active patches/cheats in the bottom-right corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Inputs
rows.desc: Shows the current controller state of the system in the bottom-left corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Texture replacements
rows.desc: Shows the status of the number of dumped and loaded texture replacements in the top-right corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Crux2 version
rows.desc: Shows the current Crux2 version.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Synchronization
rows.desc: When the emulation isn't running at 100% speed, adjusts the tempo of the audio which produces much nicer sound during fast-forward/slowdown.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Expansion
rows.desc: Determines how audio is expanded from stereo to surround for supported games.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Buffer size
rows.desc: Determines the amount of audio buffered before being pulled by the host API.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Output latency
rows.desc: How much audio is sent to the console at once. Lower means less delay; raise it if the sound crackles.

rows.heading: CONTROLS
rows.label: Standard volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the audio played on the host at normal speed.

rows.heading: CONTROLS
rows.label: Fast forward volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the audio played on the host when fast forwarding.

rows.heading: CONTROLS
rows.label: Mute all sound
rows.desc: Prevents the emulator from producing any audible sound.

rows.heading: A MEMORY CARD FOR EACH GAME
rows.label: A MEMORY CARD FOR EACH GAME

rows.heading: A MEMORY CARD FOR EACH GAME
rows.label: This game's card

rows.heading: CARD MANAGER
rows.label: Open the card manager
rows.desc: Manage memory cards and saves: copy, delete, import and export saves, and create, format or rename cards.

rows.heading: SLOT 1
rows.label: A card in the slot
rows.desc: Inserts a memory card into this slot. Off: the slot is empty.

rows.heading: SLOT 1
rows.label: Card
rows.desc: The memory card file in this slot.

rows.heading: SLOT 2
rows.label: A card in the slot
rows.desc: Inserts a memory card into this slot. Off: the slot is empty.

rows.heading: SLOT 2
rows.label: Card
rows.desc: The memory card file in this slot.

rows.heading: OPTIONS
rows.label: A memory card for each game
rows.desc: Gives every game its own memory card in slot 1, created when the game first starts.

rows.heading: OPTIONS
rows.label: A folder card shows only the running game's saves
rows.desc: Simulates a larger memory card by filtering saves only to the current game.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Backups go to
rows.desc: Where backups are saved. A network share must allow writing.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Saved states too
rows.desc: Includes save states in backups. Off: only memory cards are backed up, which is much faster.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Back up the memory cards when a game is closed
rows.desc: Backs up memory cards that changed when you close a game. The 10 newest automatic backups are kept.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Each backup replaces the one before it
rows.desc: Deletes older backups when a new one is made, so the backup folder doesn't fill up.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Back up now
rows.desc: Backs up all memory cards and save states now.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS IN SYNC
rows.label: Keep the memory cards in sync
rows.desc: Keeps memory cards in sync with the backup location each time Crux2 starts and after each game. If a card changed on both sides, the newer one is kept and the other is set aside. PCSX2 on PC and ARMSX2 on Android can use the same folder.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS IN SYNC
rows.label: Sync the memory cards now
rows.desc: Syncs the memory cards now.

rows.heading: BACKUPS ON USB DRIVE 1
rows.label: Look again
rows.desc: Refreshes the list of backups.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: Network adapter
rows.desc: Enables the network adapter for online functionality and LAN play.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: First name server
rows.desc: The DNS server games use to find their online servers. Most revival servers ask you to set their address here.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: First name server
rows.desc: The DNS server games use to find their online servers. PS2 Online and PS Rewired keep many games online; check their websites to see which supports your game.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: Second name server
rows.desc: Used when the first DNS server doesn't answer.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: Second name server's address
rows.desc: Changed number by number

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: Test the name server
rows.desc: Asks the name servers set above for the service's own website (three tries) and says whether they answer and how fast. The console's own name server is tested by the console's Settings.

rows.heading: HARD DRIVE
rows.label: Hard drive
rows.desc: Enables the internal Hard Disk Drive for expanded storage.

rows.heading: HARD DRIVE
rows.label: Make a new hard drive of 40 GB
rows.desc: The size of the drive Sony sold. An empty drive: the game, or the software that came with the drive, formats it

rows.heading: HARD DRIVE
rows.label: Make a new hard drive of 120 GB
rows.desc: For more than a few games. The file takes room only as it is written to

rows.heading: A PHONE OR A COMPUTER
rows.label: Control from a phone
rows.desc: Opens a web page (port 3311) where you can start games, manage save states and type text from your phone or computer.

rows.heading: A PHONE OR A COMPUTER
rows.label: Show the code
rows.desc: Shows the page's address as a QR code to scan with your phone.

rows.heading: A PHONE OR A COMPUTER
rows.label: A new key
rows.desc: Creates a new key. The old address stops working.

rows.heading: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
rows.label: Sign out
rows.desc: Signs out of RetroAchievements on this console.

rows.heading: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
rows.label: Sign in
rows.desc: Sign in with your retroachievements.org username and password. Your password is not stored.

rows.heading: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
rows.label: Achievements
rows.desc: When enabled and logged in, PCSX2 will scan for achievements on startup.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Say when an achievement is earned
rows.desc: Displays popup messages on events such as achievement unlocks and game completion.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: As the console's trophy notifications
rows.desc: An achievement earned is announced by the PlayStation 5 itself, as a trophy is: its notification with the badge and the trophy sound, the platinum trophy's when every achievement of the game is earned. Off: PCSX2's notice over the game, silent.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Say when a leaderboard attempt starts and ends
rows.desc: Displays popup messages when starting, submitting, or failing a leaderboard challenge.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Show achievements in progress
rows.desc: Shows icons in the screen when a challenge/primed achievement is active.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Show a leaderboard's time or score as it runs
rows.desc: Shows icons in the screen when leaderboard tracking is active.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: How long a leaderboard's notice stays

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Where the notices are shown
rows.desc: Where achievement and leaderboard notifications appear on screen.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Where the small pictures are shown
rows.desc: Where achievement progress and leaderboard trackers appear on screen.

rows.heading: MORE
rows.label: Encore mode
rows.desc: When enabled, each session will behave as if no achievements have been unlocked.

rows.heading: MORE
rows.label: Spectator mode
rows.desc: When enabled, PCSX2 will assume all achievements are locked and not send any unlock notifications to the server.

rows.heading: MORE
rows.label: Unofficial achievements
rows.desc: When enabled, PCSX2 will list achievements from unofficial sets. Please note that these achievements are not tracked by RetroAchievements, so they unlock every time.

rows.heading: SOUND EFFECTS
rows.label: Sound effects
rows.desc: Plays sound effects for events such as achievement unlocks and leaderboard submissions.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: This game's controls
rows.desc: Uses a saved controller profile for this game.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Save the controls as a profile...
rows.desc: Saves the current button mappings as a profile.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Load a profile into the controls...
rows.desc: Loads a profile's button mappings, replacing the current ones.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Make a profile with Cross and Circle swapped
rows.desc: Saves a profile with Cross and Circle swapped, for Japanese games.

rows.heading: ALL PORTS
rows.label: Put the buttons back as they were
rows.desc: Resets all controller ports and hotkeys to their default buttons.

rows.heading: SINGSTAR
rows.label: SingStar microphones
rows.desc: Uses the controller's microphone or a headset as the PS2's USB microphones, for SingStar and other singing games.

rows.heading: SINGSTAR
rows.label: Test player 1's microphone
rows.desc: Speak or sing for five seconds; it is played back to you as a game would hear it, and the boot log's "mic test" lines say how the microphone did. Close the game first

rows.heading: SINGSTAR
rows.label: Test player 2's microphone
rows.desc: Speak or sing for five seconds; it is played back to you as a game would hear it, and the boot log's "mic test" lines say how the microphone did. Close the game first

rows.heading: LIGHT GUN
rows.label: Light gun (GunCon 2)
rows.desc: Plugs a GunCon 2 into the PS2's USB port 1, or two GunCon 2s into ports 1 and 2 for two players, for light-gun games. Choose it for those games only (in their own options): a game that does not expect a light gun may not see its controller. Two guns take USB port 2, which the SingStar microphones use too.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: One or two players
rows.desc: Player 1 on port 1, player 2 on port 2, no multitap.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: Up to four players, multitap in port 1
rows.desc: Players 1 to 4 on a multitap in port 1, for most games with three or four players.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: Up to four players, multitap in port 2
rows.desc: Player 1 on port 1, players 2 to 4 on a multitap in port 2, for games that need it there.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: Light bar in the player's colour
rows.desc: Sets each controller's light bar to its player colour: blue, red, green, pink.

rows.heading: BY HAND
rows.label: Multitap in port 1
rows.desc: Enables an additional three controller slots. Not supported in all games.

rows.heading: BY HAND
rows.label: Multitap in port 2
rows.desc: Enables an additional three controller slots. Not supported in all games.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Controller
rows.desc: The controller plugged into this port.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Map it to a controller of the console
rows.desc: Every button of this port goes on the console's controller 1 (the first one, if there are fewer)

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Map it to a USB controller
rows.desc: Maps this port to a controller plugged into the console's USB port.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Invert Left Stick
rows.desc: Inverts the direction of the left analog stick.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Invert Right Stick
rows.desc: Inverts the direction of the right analog stick.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Analog Deadzone
rows.desc: Sets the analog stick deadzone, i.e. the fraction of the stick movement which will be ignored.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Analog Sensitivity
rows.desc: Sets the analog stick axis scaling factor. Modern controllers with square pickup zones, e.g. DualShock 4, Xbox One have better diagonal inputs at a range between 130-140%, but this will cause axes to reach max input early.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Use Diagonal Scale Correction
rows.desc: Transforms analog stick pickup zone from a square to a circle, allows for full input at diagonals without also scaling the X and Y axes. Ideal for modern controllers with square pickup zones, e.g. DualShock 4, Xbox One. Setting Analog Sensitivity to 100% is recommended with this setting.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Large Motor Vibration Scale
rows.desc: Increases or decreases the intensity of low frequency vibration sent by the game.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Small Motor Vibration Scale
rows.desc: Increases or decreases the intensity of high frequency vibration sent by the game.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Button/Trigger Deadzone
rows.desc: Sets the deadzone for activating buttons/triggers, i.e. the fraction of the trigger which will be ignored.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Pressure Modifier Amount
rows.desc: Sets the pressure when the modifier button is held.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 2
rows.label: Controller
rows.desc: The controller plugged into this port.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Leave a game by holding
rows.desc: Hold these buttons to leave the game.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Pressure from R2
rows.desc: For games that use pressure-sensitive buttons: how far you pull R2 sets how hard the face buttons and D-pad are pressed.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Left stick response
rows.desc: Linear: as the stick is pushed. Gentle to Gentlest: a small push moves less, for finer control near the centre; a full push still goes all the way.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Right stick response
rows.desc: Linear: as the stick is pushed. Gentle to Gentlest: a small push moves less, for finer control near the centre; a full push still goes all the way.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aim with motion
rows.desc: Aims the GunCon 2 light gun by moving the controller (always, while a GunCon 2 is plugged in). Hold R3 a moment to recentre; hold it for two seconds to measure the screen.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aim
rows.desc: Steady: where the controller points is where the gun aims, and it does not drift away. Like a mouse: the aim of before, which adds up the controller's turns and stops at the edges.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aim speed
rows.desc: How far you turn the controller to aim at the edge of the screen (steady aim). Your screen: as measured by pointing at its corners.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Measure the screen
rows.desc: Back in the game, point at the screen's top-left corner and press R3, then at its bottom-right corner and press R3. Holding R3 for two seconds in a game does the same.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aim smoothing
rows.desc: Steadies a still hand without slowing a quick sweep (steady aim).

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Holding the controller
rows.desc: Steady aim: in both hands, or stood upright in one hand with your index finger on R2 like a pistol. Either: read from how you hold it when the aim is centred.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: R2's click for the light gun
rows.desc: While a GunCon 2 is plugged in, R2 resists and then gives way like a trigger, and the shot comes with the click.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aim like a mouse: how far to turn to the edge
rows.desc: How far you need to turn the controller to aim at the edge of the screen (the aim like a mouse).

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aim with a PlayStation Move (Move Management)
rows.desc: Player 1 aims the GunCon 2 with a PlayStation Move, and a Navigation controller works its D-pad. Needs the Move Management payload running. Press Select on the Move to recentre.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: USB keyboard
rows.desc: Lets a USB keyboard type in the menus, and act as a PS2 keyboard in games that support one.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: USB controllers (experimental)
rows.desc: Lets you use controllers plugged into the console's USB ports, such as a DualShock 3, Xbox 360 pads, guitars and drums. Experimental.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Rounding mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point operations are rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Division rounding mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point division is rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Clamping mode
rows.desc: How numbers out of range are handled. Normal suits most games

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable recompiler
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of 64-bit MIPS-IV machine code to native code.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable cache (slow)
rows.desc: Enables emulation of the EE's hardware cache. Interpreter only, provided for diagnostics.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: INTC spin detection
rows.desc: Huge speedup for some games, with almost no compatibility side effects.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Wait loop detection
rows.desc: Moderate speedup for some games, with no known side effects.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable fast memory access
rows.desc: Uses backpatching to avoid register flushing on every memory access.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Pause on TLB miss
rows.desc: Pauses the virtual machine when a TLB miss occurs, instead of ignoring it and continuing.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable 128MB RAM (dev console)
rows.desc: Exposes additional memory to the virtual machine, expanding the EE and IOP memory to 128MB and 8MB respectively.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: VU0 rounding mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point operations are rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: VU1 rounding mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point operations are rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: Enable VU0 recompiler (micro mode)
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of Vector Unit 0 (VU0) microprograms to native code.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: Enable VU1 recompiler
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of Vector Unit 1 (VU1) microprograms to native code.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: mVU flag hack
rows.desc: Good speedup and high compatibility, may cause graphical errors.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: Instant VU1
rows.desc: Runs VU1 instantly. Provides a modest speed improvement in most games. Safe for most games, but a few games may exhibit graphical errors.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate floating point (FPU)
rows.desc: Does the FPU's maths exactly as the PS2 does, for games whose physics or AI go wrong otherwise. Slower. From PCSX2 Reliquary.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate floating point (VU0)
rows.desc: Does VU0's maths exactly as the PS2 does. Usually needed with the FPU one. Slower. From PCSX2 Reliquary.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate floating point (VU1)
rows.desc: Does VU1's maths exactly as the PS2 does, for some graphics errors. Much slower: use it only when a game needs it. From PCSX2 Reliquary.

rows.heading: I/O PROCESSOR (IOP, MIPS-I)
rows.label: Enable IOP recompiler
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of 32-bit MIPS-I machine code to native code.

rows.heading: GAME SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable game fixes
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies fixes to known problematic games on game start.

rows.heading: GAME SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable compatibility patches
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies compatibility patches to known problematic games.

rows.heading: GAME SETTINGS
rows.label: Recommended picture settings
rows.desc: Applies the higher blending accuracy, accurate alpha test or AA1 that the game database recommends. Settings made in a game's own options take priority.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Create save state backups
rows.desc: Creates a backup copy of a save state if it already exists when the save is created. The backup copy has a .backup suffix

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Save a state by itself
rows.desc: Automatically saves the game's state at this interval. Load it from the quick menu with "Load the auto-save". The game may pause briefly while saving.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Undo for a loaded state
rows.desc: Keeps the game's current state before you load a save state, so you can undo the load from the quick menu.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Sleep-safe saving
rows.desc: Saves the game's state when you open the PS5 menu and every five minutes, so you can continue after the console goes to rest mode.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Compression method
rows.desc: Sets the compression algorithm for savestate.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Compression level
rows.desc: Sets the compression level for savestate.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: This run
rows.desc: Shows the log of this session.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Save the log
rows.desc: Writes this session's log to crux2-boot.log now, and the rest of the session's lines as they come. For something that went wrong without Crux2 noticing.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Boot log
rows.desc: Only when something goes wrong: the session's log is kept in memory and written to crux2-boot.log after a crash, a game that did not start, 15 seconds without a new picture while a game runs, or Save the log. Always written: every line goes to the file as it is logged, as before. Takes effect the next time Crux2 starts.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: The run before
rows.desc: Shows the log of the previous session, including a crash report if it crashed.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: The emulator's own log
rows.desc: Shows the newest lines of PCSX2's own log (logs/emulog.txt).

rows.heading: TAKING THEM ALONG
rows.label: Copy the logs to USB drive 1
rows.desc: Puts the three logs in a folder named Crux2-logs there, to read on a computer or to pass on with a description of what went wrong

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: Log to a file
rows.desc: Writes log messages to emulog.txt.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: Verbose
rows.desc: Writes dev log messages to log sinks.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: Timestamps
rows.desc: Writes timestamps alongside log messages.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: EE console
rows.desc: Writes debug messages from the game's EE code to the console.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: IOP console
rows.desc: Writes debug messages from the game's IOP code to the console.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: CDVD verbose reads
rows.desc: Logs disc reads from games.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
rows.label: Enable trace logging
rows.desc: Writes the selected kinds of events to the log. Slow, and the log grows quickly.

rows.heading: GRAPHICS DEBUGGING
rows.label: Use debug blend
rows.desc: Forces SW blending and disables several optimizations.

rows.heading: GRAPHICS DEBUGGING
rows.label: GS dump length
rows.desc: How long "Record a GS dump" in the quick menu records. A heavy scene gives several hundred MB a second, even compressed.

rows.heading: GRAPHICS DEBUGGING
rows.label: GS dump compression
rows.desc: Change the compression algorithm used when creating a GS dump.

rows.heading: GRAPHICS DEBUGGING
rows.label: Dump GS draws
rows.desc: Dumps information about every draw to the snapshots folder. Very slow and very large.

rows.heading: GRAPHICS DEBUGGING
rows.label: Save frame count
rows.desc: -1 saves every frame.

rows.heading: PS5 TUNING
rows.label: Sound and controls before the emulator
rows.desc: Gives sound, controllers and menus priority over the emulator, and runs downloads and copies after it. Prevents crackling and late button presses.

rows.heading: PS5 TUNING
rows.label: Build shaders quickly first
rows.desc: Draws new effects with a quickly built shader first, then switches to the optimised one. Reduces stutter the first time an effect appears.

rows.heading: NATIVE CODE MODULES (EXPERIMENTAL)
rows.label: Use native code modules
rows.desc: Runs a game's code from a native module built with the recomp kit from your own copy of the game. Experimental.

rows.heading: NATIVE CODE MODULES (EXPERIMENTAL)
rows.label: Put executables on the share
rows.desc: Copies a game's executable to the network share when no module exists, so the recomp kit can build one.

rows.heading: NATIVE CODE MODULES (EXPERIMENTAL)
rows.label: Native code may use hardware
rows.desc: Lets native modules access the console's hardware directly. Turn off if a game hangs with its module.

rows.heading: NATIVE CODE MODULES (EXPERIMENTAL)
rows.label: Check native code
rows.desc: Runs every function twice and compares the result with PCSX2's interpreter. Very slow; for finding bugs only.

rows.heading: UPDATES
rows.label: Look for a newer Crux2
rows.desc: Checks GitHub for a newer version. Nothing is downloaded without asking.

rows.heading: UPDATES
rows.label: Look for a newer Crux2 at start-up
rows.desc: Checks GitHub for a newer version each time Crux2 starts. Nothing is downloaded without asking.

rows.heading: UPDATES
rows.label: Game fixes from GitHub at start
rows.desc: Each time Crux2 starts, fetches the game fixes that changed since this version was made (game database entries and game patches). They apply to the games started after they came.

rows.heading: UPDATES
rows.label: What's new
rows.desc: What was added, changed and fixed in each version, newest first.

rows.heading: UPDATES
rows.label: Install this version again
rows.desc: Reinstalls the newest version to repair missing or broken files. Your settings, saves and games are kept.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE
rows.label: Graphics driver on its own thread
rows.desc: Runs the graphics driver on its own CPU thread. Usually faster in demanding games.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE
rows.label: Wait for the GPU: checking for
rows.desc: How long the driver keeps checking whether the GPU is done before it starts sleeping between checks.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE
rows.label: Wait for the GPU: sleeps of
rows.desc: How long the driver sleeps between checks while waiting for the GPU.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE
rows.label: Profile the next start
rows.desc: Records detailed performance data on the next start and writes it to crux2-boot.log. Useful for finding out why a game is slow.

rows.heading: ABOUT
rows.label: Quit Crux2
rows.desc: Closes Crux2. A running game is closed first.

rows.heading: SAVE STATES
rows.label: Load Backup State From Selected Slot

rows.heading: SAVE STATES
rows.label: Save State and Select Next Slot

rows.heading: SAVE STATES
rows.label: Select Next Slot and Save State
Recommended settings
rows.desc: PCSX2's game database does not know this game

rows.label: Use the settings tested on a PS5
rows.desc: Writes the settings above as this game's own. Each can be changed or taken away again here.

rows.label: Texture pack
rows.desc: Put replacement textures for this game in textures/SLUS-00000/replacements, in the title folder or in a Crux2 or PS2 folder on a USB drive or network share. Turn on "Load textures" in Graphics to use them.

rows.label: Back to the Settings for everything
rows.desc: Removes all of this game's own settings, including its patches and cheats.

rows.label: Forget the time played
rows.desc: Played 1 h 0 min so far
